tier_reason: Discussion #567 (V2.1 announcement, 2025-04-24) states '510,308 Rectangles at 60 FPS' (TGFX) vs '34,721' (Skia) and 'at least 10 times faster than Skia's m136 version - reaching up to 16 times'; the benchmark code is public (libpag/tgfx-benchmark src/benchmark/ParticleBench.cpp and the same-source libpag/skia-benchmark src/benchmark/ParticleBench.cpp, Skia gn args in scripts/skia/build_web.js and build_mac.sh), but the device, GPU, browser and build used for the posted numbers are never stated, so first-party C, not A.

corrections.workload: ParticleBench-Rect from libpag/tgfx-benchmark and libpag/skia-benchmark (the same source with each engine's API): animated anti-aliased filled rectangles of 4-14 px (times screen density) in three colours, drawn one drawRect call each; the rectangle count ramps up every frame until FPS falls below 59.5 with average draw time above about 14.7 ms, and the count held at that point is reported. This is a GPU-backend comparison (TGFX GPU renderer vs Skia Ganesh), run in the browser via WebGL/WebAssembly at tgfx.org/benchmark or natively on Windows/macOS.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the posted numbers. Benchmark repos: TGFX built as a CMake Release target (C++17); Skia built with gn is_official_build=true is_debug=false skia_enable_ganesh=true (web build: target_cpu=wasm, skia_use_webgl=true, Emscripten).
corrections.hardware: Not stated (device, GPU and browser behind the 510,308 vs 34,721 numbers are unknown; the online benchmark runs on the viewer's own device)
corrections.caveats: First-party announcement (release notes of V2.1 dated 2025-04-24) with no GPU model, driver, OS, browser, resolution or backend for the quoted numbers; the result screenshots in the discussion sit behind private-user-images tokens and tgfx.org/benchmark is blocked from this environment (EGRESS_BLOCKED), so only the numbers quoted in the discussion text were seen. Benchmark code is public and the workload is identical on both sides (libpag/tgfx-benchmark and libpag/skia-benchmark, src/benchmark/ParticleBench.cpp; Skia built with is_official_build=true is_debug=false, Ganesh), so the comparison is GPU renderer vs GPU renderer, not a CPU rasterizer test. It is a single synthetic test of many small anti-aliased filled rectangles, which the discussion itself says covers only basic rectangle rendering; the result depends on draw-call batching more than rasterization. skia-benchmark moved to chrome/m136 on 2025-04-08 and to m142 on 2025-10-15, so today's online page compares against m142, not the m136 build behind the quoted numbers.

notes: Benchmark source found in the libpag org (tgfx-benchmark, BSD-3-Clause, last commit 2026-08-24; skia-benchmark, BSD-3-Clause): anyone can rerun it, so a rerun with a stated GPU/browser could lift this to A. Metadata checked: BSD-3-Clause, 1.6k stars, not archived, last commit 2026-09-24 (active). 510,308 / 34,721 = 14.7x (derived from page data), consistent with the '10x to 16x' wording.

tier_reason: The README 'Why?' section says verbatim that 'for Audulus, vger maintains 120fps while nanovg falls to 30fps on my 120Hz iPad because of CPU-side path tessellation, and other overhead'; this is a single first-party anecdote with no scene, iPad model, nanovg version or frame-time data, so C. The only comparison code in the repo (testNanovgPerf in Tests/vgerTests/vgerTests.mm) is commented out and no results are published.

corrections.caveats: Single anecdotal first-party figure from the README 'Why?' section for one app (the Audulus UI) on one unnamed 120Hz iPad; no nanovg version, scene description or frame-time numbers, and 120 fps is the display cap, so vger's headroom is unknown. Tests/vgerTests/vgerTests.mm has an XCTest testNanovgPerf (10,000 random quadratic bezier strokes at 512x512 through nanovg's Metal backend), but it is commented out and no results are published; the active testBezierPerf and testTigerPerf time vger alone. GPU (Metal fragment-shader) renderer vs nanovg, whose slowdown the README attributes to CPU-side path tessellation; Apple-only (iOS/macOS, Metal), with a Rust/wgpu port in audulus/vger-rs for other platforms; not a CPU rasterizer. Baseline nanovg is not Skia, Cairo or Blend2D.

notes: The number lives only in README.md 'Why?' (raw README read); hardware is just '120Hz iPad'. Implementation is Objective-C++ (.mm) plus Metal shaders with a plain C API header and C++20 in Package.swift, so the record's language field ('C') would be better as 'Objective-C++ with a C API' (not a correctable field here).
